Questions.Text: Find the index of the target value in the sorted array: [1, 3, 5, 7, 9], Target = 7
Questions.Explanation: The target value 7 is at index 3 (0-based index) in the sorted array.

Questions.Text: What is the mid index when performing binary search on array [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with left=0 and right=4?
Questions.Explanation: The mid index is calculated as left + (right - left) // 2. Here, it's 0 + (4 - 0) // 2 = 2.

Questions.Text: What happens if the middle value is greater than the target in binary search?
Questions.Explanation: When the middle value is greater than the target, binary search moves the right pointer to mid - 1 to continue searching in the left half.

Questions.Text: What is the time complexity of binary search in the worst case?
Questions.Explanation: The time complexity of binary search in the worst case is O(log n), as the search space is halved with each iteration.

Questions.Text: Binary search works only on arrays that are:
Questions.Explanation: Binary search requires the array to be sorted to determine whether to search in the left or right half.

Questions.Text: What is the space complexity of binary search when implemented iteratively?
Questions.Explanation: The space complexity of binary search implemented iteratively is O(1), as it uses a constant amount of extra space.

Questions.Text: Which of the following scenarios will binary search NOT work efficiently?
Options: Searching in a rotated sorted array
Searching for duplicate elements in a sorted array
Questions.Explanation: Binary search will not work efficiently on unsorted arrays because it depends on the data being sorted to reduce the search space.

Questions.Text: Find the first occurrence of the target value in the sorted array: [1, 3, 3, 3, 5], Target = 3
Questions.Explanation: To find the first occurrence, continue searching in the left half even after finding a match. The first occurrence of 3 is at index 1.

Questions.Text: Find the minimum element in the rotated sorted array: [5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3, 4]
Questions.Explanation: In a rotated sorted array, the minimum element is the pivot point, which is 1 in this case.

Questions.Text: What happens if binary search is applied on an unsorted array?
Options: The target may not be found even if it exists
The result depends on the target value
Questions.Explanation: Binary search may not find the target value if the array is unsorted because it relies on a sorted array to work efficiently.

Questions.Text: Find the peak element in the array [1, 2, 3, 1].
Questions.Explanation: A peak element is greater than its neighbors. Here, 3 is the peak element.

Questions.Text: What adjustment is made in binary search when searching for the last occurrence of a target?
Options: Move left pointer to mid + 1 on match
Move right pointer to mid - 1 on match
Stop searching after the first match
Use linear search after the first match
Questions.Explanation: To find the last occurrence, move the left pointer to mid + 1 on a match to continue searching in the right half.
